title: NeoMundi Evidence reconciliation map, version 1
description: An EXPLICIT table of correspondences between a receipt's labels and NeoMundi fields. Required, because deciding that a third party's score corresponds to ours is a claim about two definitions, and no extractor can make it. Without an entry, a field is NOT COMPARABLE. Une table EXPLICITE de correspondances. Exigee, parce que decider qu'un score tiers correspond au notre est une affirmation sur deux definitions.

receipt_context.description: The measurement context the RECEIPT declares. Compared with ours BEFORE any value: two values are a computation divergence only if they measure the same thing. An undeclared context makes every measured value NOT COMPARABLE -- which is the honest outcome, not a failure.

receipt_label.description: The label as the receipt writes it. NOT a key on its own: pair it with `receipt_source_path` when the receipt repeats a label.

neomundi_field.description: Must exist in our records. Targeting a field that does not is refused LOUDLY, never reported as a silent MISSING.

basis.description: WHY these two are held to correspond. Mandatory: an unexplained correspondence is a guess.

kind.description: Decides whether a comparability boundary applies. A DIGEST matches or does not: the measurement version changes nothing, and calling it NOT COMPARABLE would destroy the strongest evidence available. Only `measured_value` is context-sensitive.

requires.description: Material needed to VERIFY this field (a log, a key). If not supplied via --supplied, the field is NOT VERIFIABLE -- which is our inability to check, not a divergence.

receipt_source_path.description: The source path the importer recorded for this field. A TRUE key, unlike the label: a real receipt may carry the same label on several rows -- observed on the CP8 package, where "Verifier A" names both the vulnerable and the patched fixture. When a label matches several fields and no path is given, the field is refused as AMBIGUOUS rather than silently resolved to the first match.
